states.applied: Applied on the hosted database, with evidence recorded (here or in migrations-policy.json's appliedThroughLovable).
states.unverified: No evidence either way in this repository. Must be confirmed by the owner before release; treated as NOT applied by the guard.
states.pending: Known NOT to be applied on the hosted database yet.

$comment: RELEASE PARITY STATE. Enforced by scripts/release-parity-check.ts, which runs in CI and before a release. This file records, for every canonical migration at the release frontier, whether it is believed applied on the hosted database, and which database objects it introduces. The guard fails when application code on this branch references an object whose migration is not applied -- the exact class of failure that stopped employers saving jobs during UAT. It NEVER connects to a database, holds no credentials and applies no migration; it compares this repository against itself. Edit it deliberately: every entry is an owner-level statement about production.

frontier.note: Work-country / sub-jurisdiction on the Passport profile. Believed applied hosted under a Lovable-generated version, but this repository holds no appliedThroughLovable record for it, so it is not asserted here. Confirm before release.
Replaces sp_disclosure_payload so a disclosure renders the HOLDER's sub-jurisdiction. Same evidence gap as the migration above; confirm together with it.

THE MIGRATION THIS GUARD EXISTS FOR. Deployed application code expected these columns while the hosted schema did not have them, and employers could not save or publish a job at all. Kept here as the worked example, not as history.

Vocabulary/lifecycle data only -- introduces no object application code can reference, so it can never produce a code/schema mismatch. It still has to be applied, in order, for the audit vocabulary to be correct.

Applied hosted through the tracked Lovable route; the generated copy (20260825171344_7f6e501f-...) was left in the active migration path and is what broke clean full-history replay on origin/main. It is now recorded in migrations-policy.json's appliedThroughLovable and removed from the active path.

cd_definition_versions.content_version -> v3.1-draft-4. No new object, but NOT inert: the database stamps every new report snapshot from this row while the payload carries version.ts's CONTENT_VERSION, so shipping the code without this makes each new report disagree with itself about which wording the candidate read.

Extends the per-match profession eligibility guard to professions.ranked. Replaces an existing function rather than adding one, so a code/schema mismatch here is not a missing-object error -- it is the new candidate-facing recommendation reaching a snapshot UNVALIDATED. Apply before, or with, the code that writes `ranked`.
cd_definition_versions.content_version -> v3.1-draft-5. Same reasoning as the draft-4 migration above.
Two cig_professions rows. Data only: the picker reads whatever rows exist, so the code does not name them and cannot break without them -- the profession list is simply shorter.

evidenceBaseline.note: Every canonical migration at or below this version has a recorded hosted application in migrations-policy.json and is therefore treated as applied without needing an entry below. Nothing above it is assumed.
